items.q: He introduced me to Clark Monroe, he introduced me to Don Redman. He introduced me to Duke.

ctx.x: New York Cotton Club, yes. And it was full of chorus girls around St. Louis, testing chorus girls, you know, Claudia Oliver, that fantastic dancer. Joe "Ziggy" Johnson was producing the shows there at the time. It was a big club, you know. And all the big musicians that would come through there with Fletcher Henderson and all the other bands, they knew somebody that was in the Jester-Pillars band because they had been big musicians themselves; Sidney Catlett knew Walter Johnson who used to come through there with…

items.title: Harry "Sweets" Edison interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: Don Redmond was playing across the street at 132nd Street

ctx.x: I couldn’t miss it. I couldn’t go to bed. I lived on 130th and Seventh Avenue. Art Tatum was playing on 131st Street, Don Redmond was playing across the street at 132nd Street, Billie Holiday was singing at 138th Street at a place called the Yeah Man Club, there was Small’s Paradise on 135th Street. Everything was in Harlem. You know you could walk, and I walked so much ‘till I just passed out. I just couldn’t miss anything. So everybody was, you could see everybody that you wanted to see in the daytime on…

Club. It was just, it was amazing and it held my, I was just in awe at all of these people that I had seen on the stage in Columbus, Ohio at a dance. Cab Calloway. Here I am walking down Seventh Avenue, and looking at these people and saying hello to them. And Count Basie introduced me to all these people. He was like a father. When I first joined the band I was 19 and he just took a liking to me and he introduced me to Ellington, James P. Johnson, Art Tatum, Louis Armstrong, oh my goodness. It was just…

items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Don Redman and his band used to come to that theater, the Connie’s Inn Revue.

ctx.x: Did you get to meet him at that time?

No, I didn’t get to meet him because they hurried me from backstage, I wasn’t supposed to be there anyway, because this was an all-white theater but black performers used to perform there. Like, they used to have the Cotton Club Revue there downtown, and we weren’t even allowed in the balcony. The Cab Calloway show used to come there from the Cotton Club. Duke Ellington’s show used to come there from the Cotton Club. Don Redman and his band used to come to that theater, the Connie’s Inn Revue. But if they didn’t…
